newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil steady despite crude.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil steady despite crude.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps were steady at midday on Monday in quiet trading despite another hike to crude prices on Friday as the market remained rangebound in the absence of fresh indicators, traders said.
"The market is not going anywhere right now. We need a new wave of buying or massive selling to break this range," said a trader.
June gas oil swaps were quoted unchanged from Friday at $25.10/$25.30 per barrel, brokers said.
On Friday June Brent crude closed up 24 cents to $18.93 per barrel on the International Petroleum Exchange.

The swaps market has been large affected by the narrow range of physical trade over the past two weeks where deals were done at between $25.00 and $25.50 per barrel on a free-on-board basis, traders said,
"Everytime there is an offer below $25.50, someone comes out to buy and the bids are never below $25.00," a trader said.

Traders said the absence of arbitrage exports from the West for second half June arrival are keeping prices steady but prices are not rising because of ample supplies from regional sources amid weak demand.
Fuel oil was quoted in a wide range as uncertainties crept into the market after last week's strong rally.
June fuel oil swaps were last quoted at $100.50/$102.00 per tonne, down from Friday's $102.00/$103.00, brokers said.
June traded up to a high of $102.50 on Friday, they said.
Traders said the market is reassessing the value of fuel oil after its more than $5.00 per tonne rise in one week as physical sellers emerge in wake of this big price hike.
Also traders said there are some nagging worries among some players if the envisaged buying spree of a local trader would actually take place.
